$comment: Shared ladder fixture, consumed by BOTH ports: android MorseLadderTest and ios MorseKitCheck. Data, not code — see CLAUDE.md's two-ports rule.

derivation.studyOrder: kochOrder, then pickablePunctuation filtered to the opted-in set, in pickable order
derivation.note: This is the divergence that made the item: Android threaded opted-in punctuation through the studyOrder ladder while iOS added it straight to the active set, so unlocking singles->pairs took 40 characters on one port and 37 on the other. The ladder is the intended design. Opting in adds a mark to the LADDER, not to the active set — it still has to be reached and mastered.
derivation.optOut: activeAfter = activeBefore with every pickablePunctuation character NOT in selectedPunctuation removed, relative order preserved; removed = those characters, in activeBefore order. Only pickable punctuation is ever removed: '?' is Koch core and stays, and a mark that was never earned is simply not there to remove. Opting back IN changes nothing here - the mark goes back on the studyOrder ladder (cases above), not into the active set. The mark's CharacterStats entry is kept on both ports (behavioural check, not fixture data).
derivation.optOutNote: Issue #133: opting out used to leave an earned mark in the drill. Decided: it is removed from the active set and its stats are kept, so opting back in and re-earning it loses no history.

optOutCases.name: earned all three, opt out of the comma
earned all three, opt out of everything
earned the period only, opt it out ('?' is Koch core and stays)
marks never earned have nothing to remove
opting back in is not an immediate add
